t: Saharan Berber reformists who built an empire from the Senegal River to the Ebro, ruled from Marrakesh.
Their victory at Sagrajas in 1086 halted Castile's advance and kept much of al-Andalus Muslim for generations.
Overstretched on two fronts, they fell to the Almohads, who used the same charge of impiety the Almoravids once used.
dyk: The Almoravid gold dinar was so trusted that Christian Iberia imitated it as the morabetino, the origin of the Castilian maravedí.
ev: Almoravids capture Sijilmasa, northern terminus of the trans-Saharan gold trade
Marrakesh is founded as the capital of the northern branch
Yusuf ibn Tashfin shatters Alfonso VI's army at the Battle of Sagrajas
Almoravids absorb the taifa kingdom of Seville
Death of Yusuf ibn Tashfin, the empire's greatest ruler
Alfonso I of Aragon takes Zaragoza
Tashfin ibn Ali dies near Oran, opening Morocco to the Almohads
Almohads storm Marrakesh and kill the last Almoravid ruler, Ishaq ibn Ali

f.founder: Abdallah ibn Yasin, Yusuf ibn Tashfin
